## The Great Patriotic War (1941-1945AD), the Holocaust, Refined Leningrad Siege Zone (Region 17), and the 1946-1947AD Famine

Across the western and southern regions of our 45-region partition (Regions 1-17, 21, 22, 27 and 29), the Great Patriotic War (1941-1945AD), the Holocaust, post-war population exchanges (1944-1948AD) and the 1946-1947AD famine left deep, lasting demographic scars (Table \ref{tab:wwii-postwar}).
Byelorussian SSR (Region 6: Western Belarus & Region 7: Eastern BSSR): Occupied from June 1941AD to July 1944AD, Belarus lost 2,2M to 2,5M inhabitants (~25% of its population), including ~750k to 800k Jews murdered in the Minsk Ghetto (~100k), Maly Trostenets, Brest/Bronnaya Gora (~50k), Grodno, Pinsk, Vitebsk, Mogilev and Gomel, and 628 villages (such as Khatyn) burned with all inhabitants ([archived PDF](papers/soviet_belarus_wwii_demography_2004_1.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/soviet_belarus_wwii_demography_2024_2.pdf)) [@bylov2004belarus; @korsak2024belarus; @arad2009holocaust]. Region 7 fell by -28,5% from 5 850k (1941AD) to 4 180k (1945AD, 4 890k in 1953AD), while Region 6 dropped by -28,1% from 2 950k (1941AD) to 2 120k (1945AD, 2 310k in 1953AD) as ~274 200 ethnic Poles were transferred to Poland under the 1944-1946AD Lublin treaties.

Ukrainian SSR (Regions 8-14): Combined population across Ukrainian Regions 8-15 plunged by -11 410k (-27,5%) from 41 560k (1941AD) to 30 150k (1945AD), driven by ~6,8M to 8,0M war deaths (including ~1,5M to 1,6M Holocaust victims at Babyn Yar in Kyiv 33 771, Kamianets-Podilskyi 23 600, Lviv/Janowska & Belzec, Drobytsky Yar in Kharkiv, and Romanian-occupied Odesa/Transnistria), 2,4M *Ostarbeiter* deportations and eastern evacuation ([archived PDF](papers/soviet_holocaust_occupied_ussr_2026_1.pdf)) [@arad2009holocaust; @kornilova2026aktsiya1005; @mesle2012mortalite]. In Region 8 (Galicia & Volhynia: 7 740k in 1941AD -> 5 180k in 1945AD, -33,1%), the Holocaust (~700k murdered) was followed by the 1944-1946AD Polish-Ukrainian population exchange (~810 000 Poles transferred from Western Ukraine to Poland and ~482 800 Ukrainians transferred from Poland into Ukraine, plus ~140k Ukrainians deported inside Poland during 1947AD *Operation Vistula*) and the NKVD deportation of ~203 000 Western Ukrainians accused of aiding the OUN-UPA insurgency (culminating in Operation *Zapad* in October 1947AD, which exiled 77 791 people in three days to Karaganda, Omsk, Kemerovo and Vorkuta) [@polian2001against; @zemskov2003spetsposelentsy; @statiev2010borderlands]. In Region 9 (Northern Bukovina, Budjak & Transcarpathia: 2 780k in 1941AD -> 1 920k in 1945AD), Transcarpathia (Zakarpattia / Uzhhorod) was ceded by Czechoslovakia on 29 June 1945AD [@polian2001against].

Refined Region 17 (Leningrad Siege Metropolis, Novgorod, and Pskov Oblasts): Separated cleanly from Kaliningrad Oblast (Region 5), Region 17 isolates the pure demographic shock of the 872-day Siege of Leningrad (8 September 1941AD - 27 January 1944AD) and the scorched-earth Wehrmacht occupation of Novgorod and Pskov ([archived PDF](papers/soviet_leningrad_siege_demography_2026_1.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/soviet_leningrad_siege_demography_2019_2.pdf)) [@lomagin2002neizvestnaya; @boldovsky2019leningrad; @kulish2026leningrad]. Between September 1941AD and January 1944AD, 800 000 to 1 000 000 civilians starved or froze to death inside Leningrad while 1,74M residents (including ~89k Leningrad Germans and Ingrian Finns deported to Siberia and the Lena Delta) were evacuated across Lake Ladoga's *Road of Life*, shrinking the city from 3,19M (1939AD) to 546k in January 1944AD (920k by late 1945AD), while Novgorod (40k in 1939AD -> fewer than 3k civilians at liberation in January 1944AD, 19k in 1945AD) and Staraya Russa were reduced to rubble. Consequently, Region 17 plunged by -56,5% from 6 960k in June 1941AD to 3 030k in 1943AD, recovering via re-evacuation and the 1944-1945AD border transfers of Ivangorod/Pechory (from Estonia) and Pytalovo/Abrene (from Latvia) to 4 340k in 1945AD (-37,6%) and 5 490k in 1953AD (still -21,1% below 1941AD, further battered politically during the 1949-1950AD "Leningrad Affair").

Frontline Russian Regions 21, 22, 27 and 29 and the 1946-1947AD Post-War Famine: Along the Smolensk-Rzhev-Vyazma-Bryansk axis, Region 21 (Upper Volga & Western Front) dropped by -25,8% (13 280k in 1941AD -> 9 850k in 1945AD, 10 790k in 1953AD); Region 22 (Central Black-Earth Belt: Voronezh, Kursk, Oryol) fell by -25,3% (13 850k -> 10 350k); and Region 27 (Saratov, Stalingrad & Astrakhan) fell by -19,3% (4 250k -> 3 430k, with Stalingrad reduced from 445k to 32k in February 1943AD). Immediately after the war, the severe 1946AD drought across Moldavia, Ukraine, the Central Black-Earth Belt, the Lower Volga and West Siberia  -  compounded by 17,5M tonnes of state grain procurements, grain exports and the September 1946AD removal of 27,5M rural inhabitants from state bread rationing  -  triggered the 1946-1947AD Soviet Famine (1,0M to 1,5M total excess deaths: 115k-200k in the Moldavian SSR Region 4 [2 080k in 1945AD -> 1 940k in 1947AD], ~300k-500k across Ukraine Regions 9, 10, 11 and 14 [Region 11: 6 750k -> 6 720k], and ~500k-700k across Russia Regions 21, 22, 27, 29, 35 and 38 [Region 22: 10 350k -> 10 250k]) before late Stalinist demographic recovery carried the 45-region total to 165 350k in March 1953AD ([archived PDF](papers/soviet_famine_1946_1947_2012_1.pdf); [archived PDF](papers/soviet_lenin_stalin_moldavia_famine_casu_2020.pdf)) [@zima1996golod; @ellman2000famine1947; @casu2020famine1947; @laperdin2012westsiberia1947; @laperdin2013omsk1947].
